key_insight: TRCGL-Net combines synthetic tail-class image generation, feature/attention refinement, and label-co-occurrence graph modeling to improve long-tailed chest X-ray multi-label classification.
clinical_relevance: It may help AI systems recognize rare chest X-ray findings more reliably, reducing performance gaps between common and uncommon diseases.
method: Text-guided conditional diffusion generates realistic tail-class chest X-rays with disease-semantic constraints
Channel reweighting and class-aware attention emphasize lesion-relevant features and regions
Graph convolution models label co-occurrence to share information across disease categories
evidence_signal: On the PadChest dataset, the method reports tail-class mAP 0.4904, overall mAP 0.4408, and mAUC 0.8989, outperforming prior methods.
watch_item: Synthetic data and label-co-occurrence modeling may improve performance in the studied dataset, but generalization and clinical validation across other hospitals and populations remain important concerns.
paper_title: TRCGL-Net: A Long-Tailed Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classification Framework with Generative Data Augmentation and Label Co-Occurrence Modeling
